Cloudbuilt is a fast-paced, action-adventure platformer with a focus on speed and parkour to manuever around the environment. Cloudbuilt is a fresh concept that could expand on the slowly increasing "parkour-platformer" genre. But, does the game hold up in the long run?
GAMEPLAY:
The gameplay of this game consists of platforming and using parkour to reach a goal. You use a jetpack that allows you to boost your character and give them momentum. There are also enemies which are in your way which you can defeat using a gun given to you. The controls feel tight and responsive. One of the complaints I have with this game is that the way your character controls feels floaty. It leads to too many deaths due to the controls. Another complaint I have with this game is the enemies. The whole concept of enemies in this game deducts a two points on the review scale. The problem with the enemies is your weapon, a laser gun that you can charge, and the enemy types. The laser gun does too little damage per hit and charging the weapon feels like it does the same damage as not charging it. The enemies consist of a crawling enemy, a turret, a laser beam, a laser turret that shoots 5 flat beams, and an enemy that spawns homing enemies. The turret and crawling enemies feel fair and balanced. All other enemies feel annoying and destroy the fun, especially the laser turret and the exploding enemy spawner. These 2 elements combined destroys the pacing as you constantly need to stop to kill the enemies to peacefully proceed to the next platforming challenge. Another annoying aspect of the enemies is the shield they produce if you are far enough. The problem is that sometimes the game decides to permanently give them a shield, WHICH MAKES IT EVEN HARDER TO PROGRESS. Also, the lives system is also annoying as the game is HARD, like REALLY HARD. Which means that you will be dying a lot. Overall, its gameplay is great but the enemies, character movement, and lives system hold it back from being a great game.
STORY:
Honestly, this game doesn't need one. The story is non-existent and extremely confusing as none of the characters in the game explain what is going on. The game doesn't even give the main characters name from what I heard (although, I could be wrong). The levels also have no plot relevance whatsoever besides the first level. The story tries to present it self through a log that can be accessed from the main hub. Overall, the game is completely fine without a story, but it is nice that the developers decided to include a story in a game that doesn't need one.
GRAPHICS:
The game is great looking, not much to say. The game decides to adopt the borderlands/Telltale game style with cell-shaded graphics that adopt a mature tone. The game runs smoothly with little stutter. Overall, the game has pretty solid graphics.
CONCLUSION:
Cloudbuilt is a good game, not great by any standard but still a decent experience. I suggest you wait for a price drop or sale since the 20$ price tag is not worth the game. Here are the results:

I absolutely love FTL. I wish I had more time to give this game, but I will just have to be happy that I've gotten any amount with it at all.
FTL could probably be described as a rougelite: an experience that every time you go through, is different. While the basic structure is the same, the choices and obstacles you face are different every time. My favorite aspect was probably trying to get through all of the objectives required to unlock the different ships and the different layouts.
I probably only beat the game maybe...5 times? It is brutal and takes no prisoners. Whenever I thought I was prepared to face just about anything I almost always found myself in a new area with 5 baddies aboard my ship and killing all of my crew members. It was disheartening, to be sure, but I always picked myself back up and started from square one.
While the mechanics are nothing ground-breaking, I do like the real-time/pausing action. It gives you the opportunity to set up your attacks at your leisure, then react to your opponent with plenty of time to figure out how you're going to get out of the current garbage-pile of a situation you find yourself in. And sometimes, I would argue it is necessary to be able to control the flow of time, as I would often have to align my shots to all fire simultaneously in order to pierce some of the stronger shields, and if I had to manage all of that in real-time I would definitely lose my cool, always.
All in all, while I don't think I ever found myself feeling particularly empowered, I enjoyed the atmosphere and the experience this game has to offer a ton.
Numerical value: 9.5/10
P.S. The OST is phenomenal!

Anomaly Warzone Earth is the first in a line up of great Sci-Fi/Action/Strategy games. You plan your route carefully with planning and thought, after you get to choose the loadout of vehicles you wish, after you try and survive the terrors of the Alien lifeforms which has taken over Baghdad and other ares round that part. Overall it makes me feel like I am playing a tower defense game, but instead of planning to defend whatever I need, I am actually moving through, while the Alien lifeforms is planning its way on defending either its power cores or just trying to ruin your day by just shooting you non-stop. Overall the graphics and music are great, the voice acting is good and the story is actually quite a good story, kinda weird as I was just expecting soldiers trying to move their way through either a group of terrorists or shooting their way through to get out of Baghdad, like Jagged Alliance or Doorkickers.
The game is great, short, but challenging as you may die a lot for poor planning, but thankfully their is a good checkpoint system where if you die or want to start over again, you can just start from the checkpoint. A great first game from 11 Bit Studios!

If you are completely new to worms games: Worms is a turn based strategy game where your soldiers are cute little worms. There are different weapons to annihilate your enemies and each team can have 2,3 or 4 members in the battlefield.
I have looked for the best worms game on the internet through the reviews and ended up buying worms reloaded. I do not know other worms games, they can be fun as well, but here are the reasons why this game is cool.
- There are like 40 different wepons (some are unlockable with coins that come from campaing)
- Worms are highly customizable, their look and speech has different options. I think you can even load your own audio files for their speeches
- Level designs are giving you lots of options when combined with different game styles. You can create a map with lots of explosives and traps and create a non explosive weapons game style and it becomes a tactical warfare. Or create a map with no obstacles and go for all explosives. Some weapons can be locked for spesific count of turns.
- Multiplayer is solid. I am able to play with friends with no issues. Game also looks crash free.
- You don't have to buy dlc packages to have fun in this game. DLC packages are mostly new missions.
And there is no downside of this game as far as i see. I said in the beginning, you may find the features above in another worms game but this one seems to have everything for this kind of game.

Cloudbuilt is a great game. I bought it on sale without any expectations and was blown away.
I only have 2.1 hours on record when I wrote this, so I can’t judge about the story line. My game time isn’t the only reason for that. Every level you complete gives you a different part of the story, but not in a chronological way. My strategy is to first complete the game and afterwards check out the story (yes, that is possible).
Now about the gameplay. Some levels can be played quite casually, you can take your time and check your path before you walk it and scout for enemies. But that is not the way to play this game. The purpose is to reach the end of a level with using as little time as possible, with as little deaths as possible. So you have to rush through the levels, while trying to receive 0 damage, while trying not to fall and while trying to kill your opponents. By rushing I mean really, really rushing. This game is fast and therefore the difficulty of the game can be hard.
The graphics are nice. The game is designed like a comic and it’s pulling it off very well (think in the direction of Borderlands or XIII).
I miss a multiplayer option though, In my opinion it would be great to do a real-time time attack through a level. I can also picture a last man standing game type. You know, stuff like that…
In short: Hard game (but I like a challenge) and it looks great. Although it lacks multiplayer I really recommend this game.

Easily my favourite Final Fantasy title and one of my favourite games of all time, so I was pretty excited to see it ported to PC with some touched up sprites. The base game is a solid 9.5/10 for me (because I'm a picky ♥♥♥♥♥ and nothing is perfect), but this will mostly be a review on the port more than the actual game.
Pros:
-It's still Final Fantasy IX
-The redone sprites, portraits and icons look very nice, especially the items in the menus
-The keyboard controls are easy to get acquainted with and don't feel too awkward
-The game autosaves on every screen which can make getting wiped by a boss a lot more forgiving, though I'd still recommend hard saving at Moogles for the sake of security and so you don't get trapped at a boss cutscene with no health or bad ability set-ups
Cons:
-A LOT of the sounds are bugged or broken, at least for me. I first noticed that enemy death sounds weren't playing, then I noticed that other miscellaneous sounds weren't working properly, such as the Chocobo cries and some abilities (Freya's White Draw, for example, has developed an odd chime at the beginning of the ability cast). The major sound issues are my biggest gripe about the port but thankfully the music seems to work just fine and I haven't had any issues with sounds in FMV sequences
-The static backgrounds weren't retouched and they look very blurry compared to the HD sprites walking around on them
MIxed:
-The RNG seems really wonky (for lack of a better word); steal rates range from getting the best items first to no items after 15+ attempts, Tetra Master seems to heavily favour the opponent and there are sections of the map where I can run without encounters for almost five solid minutes, such as the Conde Petie Mountain Path
Overall I'd highly recommend buying this game. I got it on sale because I'm thrifty that way but it's my third or fourth time buying the game over my lifetime so there's that. This port gets an 8/10 may well end up buying yet again someday if it gets released on PS4 or something. Maybe if it does the sounds won't be bugged and the backgrounds will be redone in HD. The game follows a semi-linear structure, where the story goes on in chapters, those that you have to complete tasks one after other directly, but most of time you can also drive or walk around the little Empire Bay, but there's not much to do on it. Story? Quite good. The game shows the rise (and almost decline) of Vito Scaletta, a guy that after getting shot in WWII, is sent back to home, where he tries to take care of his mother and sister, and solve debts left by his father. However, after doing some jobs with his old friend
Joe, he get itself involved with mafia mobs and then, he objectives goes higher: he tries to get rich and to be someone powerful in town, doing something that his father couldn't. But during his journey, he meet wrong guys, kill wrong people, and do lot's of things that he shouldn't. It's a good tale, with some flaws, but still very enjoyable.

I played this game in Windows 10, where it first wasn't opening thanks to NVidia PhysX, that also brought some problems to me while in-game. Also, MAFIA II crashed a few times when I was playing, some of those crashes was between cutscenes and this might be a deal breaker depending on what cutscene is.
And then there's the DLCs; there's 4 clothes pack and three mission packs; while I used some clothes provided on Vegas Pack, others are kind of bad, and the missions packs can be fun, but they get repetitive and bland fast, since it's almost the same thing everytime. So, there's not motive to get DLCs unless you really want more of MAFIA or just have all content library for it.
To end it all, we might know what happened to Vito in MAFIA III, so, until it releases in October:

This is quite an odd case of a game that succeeds on gameplay and then fails in the story that its trying to tell.
The gameplay is devided into
1) Car chases with more realistic collision mechanics then GTA and Saints Row, meaning that a frontal collision is going to kill you not just mildly slow down your car
2) Cover based third person shooter which is well executed.
Sadly, the story is A) completely linear and B) could be described as "Why working for Mafia sucks". On one hand, it's a real wholesome message for the kid that is trying to figure out his future occupation by playing job simulators ("Mommy, I don't want to be Mayor because City Builder X-s servers kept crashing on me!"). On the other hand, if you are wierdo like me who plays games to have fun you are going to find very little of that here as the game becomes increasingly more depressive. This is compounded by the fact that you have no sense of agency while you are helplessly observing your character making dumb decisions and throwing his life away.
FINAL VERDICT: If you are looking to have fun, this ain't the game to do it.

- The level design is amazing. Tons of multiple pathways and interesting gimmicks- I've had this game for over a year now and I'm still discovering new pathways and faster routes
- replayability. I've played Rooftop Run modern more times than I can count and I've put 60+ hours into a game that only takes about 4 hours to complete on your first playthrough.
- Graphics and presentation. I'm a sucker for good graphics and music and this game is gorgeous. (This version is the best version of this game graphically) The voice acting is also pretty good for Sonic standards- although I'm not a fan of some of the voices (personal thing xD) All the cutscenes are nicely animated which is good. And the soundtrack is fantastic. Almost every remix is great and some are even better than the original songs.
- Mod support. Some of the mods that the community have created are amazing and really are worth checking out- my personal favorite being Unleashed project (being the Unleashed fangirl that I am)
Negatives:
-The story is very underplayed and you can tell that Sonic Team had to cut out a lot of content. For example, at the end of Chemical Plant and Green Hill, Sonic and Tails stop and reflect on the stage that they just ran through. This never happens again and would really have added to the overall plot of the game. For an anniversary title that's really kinda disappointing.
- The final boss. I won't spoil it but it really sucks
- Not really a fan of Planet Wisp Act 1 tbh I think it's a bit too long for a Sonic level. And the remix isn't really the best. This is especially disappointing because I loved Planet Wisp in Colors, but it's just not that great here. Oh, and it's kind of an underwhelming last level in general.
- The game is a bit short- about 4 hours long. While this is better than purposley padding out the game (The Werehog) but for some this might be a bad thing- especially if you're not really into replaying levels for better ranks.
- And imo S ranking is waaay too easy.
But overall, this is my favorite Sonic game for a reason, I can recommend this to almost anyone. I gave this to a friend of mine for Christmas- he's not even a Sonic fan and he loves it. If you haven't played a Sonic game and have no idea where to start- this is the perfect place to begin.

Oh boy, where do I start?
First of all, I marked recieving this product for free because it was gifted to me by a friend, and as of now I haven't paid for another copy, though I plan to buy one Secondly, I've never played a Sonic game in my life, so I'm afraid I can't relate to all the nostalgia everybody gets from this game. But, with that said, I'm still absolutely obsessed with it! I'm honestly surprised I haven't played a platforming game of this genre sooner! I'm usually not one to play through a game's plot more than once, but this game has me coming back to it time and time again. If I have a few minutes to spare, I'll often spend them here.
So from what I grasp, this game is almost a fusion of various classic games. It uses Sonic as a basis, but has elements that relate to Megaman (combat, soundtrack, and
), Gunstar Heroes (bosses). I also got hints of Metroid with the soundtrack towards the end, and though somewhat irrelevant, I got vague Cave Story flashbacks with a few plot elements in the final levels.
On that note, the plot is nothing to sneeze at. The voice acting isn't the greatest, and sometimes a bit lackluster, but it has some extremely good moments too. The villians are exceptionally done, however some of the main characters feel a bit underdeveloped (I'm looking at you, Milla). I would have to say though, back on the subject of "good moments" in the plot, it really excels emotionally. There are some exceptionally dark, heartbreaking moments and some really touching, heartwarming moments that coupled with the voice acting make it difficult for even the most hardened person to not feel anything. Honestly its these moments where the voice acting REALLY shines.
The soundtrack is phenomenal. I swear one of the many reasons I keep coming back to this game is just so I can hear those tracks on loop again. As afore mentioned, it feels like a cross between Megaman and Sonic with some slight hints of Metroid vibes towards the final stages. I don't own the soundtrack as of now, but I plan to purchase it when I gather up enough money. Definitely worth the price alone.
I can't say much about the gameplay because I have nothing to compare it to, but I can definitely say it has an emphasis on speedrunning. Levels are built with a focus on trying to blast through them and taking the most efficient routes, and might I add it's very well done. The more you play, the more you understand the level layouts and the faster the route you can take. It's the old "practice makes perfect" situation. Your first time playing a level, you'll probably run into a lot of enemies you don't see on screen. Playing through the game the first time might take a few hours, but after you remember them being there, you'll be able to easily avoid them and the speedrunning elements start to become more noticeable. You'll go from beating it in 3 hours to just 1!
It should also be noted that the achievements in this game are actually very reasonable. Challenging, but its entirely possible to 100% the game without it feeling too impossibly tedious (well, except maybe Gem Hoarder). One cool thing is a lot of the achievements are earned for discovering small exploits in the game that you would've otherwise not known about. Some of which are really helpful for speedrunners. I can't tell if these were intentional or not, but they might have just been flaws left in the game because the game is so focused on speedrunning, and the developers know how much speedrunners love to find exploits. Either way, I wish more games would work like that.
In short, I highly recommend this game. Whether you are a Sonic fan or not, it's definitely worth your time and way too underrated for what its worth!

To start this review off, I have only played Lilac's adventure mode. Keep that in mind.

I enjoyed how engaging the story of the game is. It can suck you in, and get you attached to the characters. Though complicated, it ends up having a satisfying conclusion.

I had a hard time enjoying the main gameplay of the game. Though it does well at parts to make you feel like you're going fast, it interrupts this with a combat system that works horribly, and it ends up making the game feel like Super Smash Bros. Brawl's Subspace Emissary Story Mode, which had many situations which the game engine wasn't made for. (The original game was a brawler, so having platforming mixed with stun mechanics really made it difficult to traverse.) Freedom Planet feels like this in the end, which is pretty disappointing.
Another part I wanted to mention, is that this game doesn't have tutorials. Because of this, it throws you into situations, where you have no idea what to do. It forces the player to continue experimenting with whatever they have, even if it takes three minutes to even get a small understanding of what to do, let alone master it.

The boss fights of the game are at times, unbearable. You have some boss fights where you die consistently in the least fair ways, and other boss fights which are fun and enjoyable that don't punish the player. These two different kinds of boss fights mix, and at times,  you take longer on the fight than you did on the level. These boss fights aren't very organized on difficulty, and can throw you into a situation you aren't prepared for.

An excellent visual novel! That kind of game you can't stop playing once you've started. The story is fast paced and keeps you on the edge all the time, but it doesn't mean it looses on interesting details and hints.
Characters are varied, and all of them have their own stories and points of view. And they are clearly not as black and white as it may seem at the beginning.
It seems to have a lot of replayability too, because of the different choices you can make all along the way, but that I won't verify until the whole story is out, since I want to keep my first feeling choices all along on my first playthrough.
And another bonus point, the art and music are gorgeous and make the story really immersive.
Perhaps it would be even more if the characters' artworks, or at least the small portraits in the text boxes were give multiple expressions/emotions, but I can understand how difficult it is, and not all visual novels have that, so it doesn't tarnish the experience anyway.
Overall, this is an excellent game, and I hope the next chapters will be out soon.

There is a category of game that is underated by most of the gamers,   The city builder simulation...
How is it posiible to make fun by building and managing a city.   Playing a political character and try to get the most vote from the citizen.

First, they are gonna share the demand in residential, commercial and industrial zones.
Seconly, you will be able to make deal between the cities (buying electricity, selling garbage, ...)
Finaly, when you'll become a master in creating a small town,  you'll be able to create large cities of residentials area connected to other cities that will be providing power, water, garbage disposal ...

Anomaly: WE is a great example of a tower offense (reverse tower defence, of course) game.
The main storyline follows certain earth cities as they is attacked by aliens following crash landings. A good enough premise for this type of game and it follows through well.
The level of difficulty increases in a nice linear fashion, and it's not too jarring a difference between levels. Amnd the wide array of usable vehicles makes for a good strategic challenge.
I used both keyboard/mouse and controller (xbox), and I found that both work well, but it does feel more comfortable with the controller.
The graphics in this game are very good., taking a top-down approach, and still retaining a slight tilt to emphasize the 3 dimensions of the environment.
The sound in this game is ok. The voicing can be a bit annoying at times, alongs the lines of "army-esque cheering banter" whenever a successful attack is made. But you can turn that off and just use subtitles for the important dialogue.
Once you have completed the main storyline, you can be sure of still having a lot to do with extra bonus levels and different modes to try.
I found no issues or bugs while playing this game.
Definitely worth a buy if either you like tower defense, or even if you're completely new to the genre (like I was).

This is a marvelous 3D take on the Megaman style platformer, similar to Deadcore with a few elements of Mirror's Edge thrown in. Where the Blue Bomber never really transitioned to 3D with much success, these games take the helm and basically open it up for another generation. Yeah, completely different aesthetics and artstyle, but the core remains very similar, just in a wild imaginative artstyle in three dimensions. Deadcore is definitely the closest comparison. Both are excellent games deserving of your cash.
The crazy thing is both games slipped under my radar for a year or more. Hard to believe with how many games I own. The marketing for these smaller titles I hope gets a slight boost on Steam sales now and then. There is no question about it, if you like platformers and are not afraid of the 3D transition, this game is excellence incarnate.
The soundtrack is decent ambient, the voiceovers are okay to good, and the storyline is fairly vague but passable and interesting at times. 4K on ultra looks gorgeous with the cell-styled art here. Controllers are fully supported. I'm using a DS4 with Input Mapper and there are plenty of options to tune your aim and sensitivities.
All in all a solid success. Wish more people knew about it.

I bought this one on sale for less than 10€ and really dodged a bullet - for not wasting more on this absolute tat of a game.
This is by far the worst mage game I have seen in a very long time, it makes every mistake a game designer possibly could make.
To start with the player is extremely weak. Bosses will kill you in 3 hits and average enemies will spam you down in about 10, which equals ~2 seconds of taking damage. You are meant to use your pathetic 3m long lodges (only 3 of them every 10 seconds or so) or your shield, which slows you down to a crawl (considering you already move at the speed of a drunk snail, this is basically stationary), and blocks 50% damage at most. You can counter attacks by timing the shield, but as you are being attacked by 8+ enemies simultaneously, that is as useful as a rowboat in an ocean. With no paddles.
Furthermore there is zero variety in gameplay. You can choose between different colours for your spells but if you think this crafting system is gonna turn your kinetic AoE into a gravity well that pulls enemies inwards, that you can shock for some crazy combo? No. You can prime enemies with any element, using Mastery or Control attunement (very logical), and then use any Destruction charged spell to detonate. Damage is not controlled by how well you use the spells, but rather by the stats on them. And stats it has. You will collect hundreds of blobs that add the glorious "+11% fapping time" to you jerk off spell. So in the end you will end up with a spell that takes half a screen to display it's stats, but is the same fireball as that other one you had. It just pumps out bigger numbers.
Then also the enemies are all exactly the same. Melee guys, ranged guys and support guys. They mindlessly charge at you using their enormous health to tank your "Ultramega testosterone-powered oldspiceguy glorious battlespells" like it was nothing. Average fighting time is around 5-10 minutes per area (well, sometimes its 2 minutes, but feels like 10, because you always do the same thing), and if you die, you get set back half a level and have to do all the spam all over again. Every fight is basically kiting the enemies as they charge at you. No combos, no skill, or tactic will make it go any faster. Stats might, once you grind enough, but why would you?
Of course this is a railroaded magic FPS and has no story to speak of (well none that would make you care anyway). I was told the woman is being voiced by some big celebrity. I am told I should care. I can't find a reason why. Basically you get screwed over by a cult and go off to kill hordes of the same bad guys because revenge and♥♥♥♥♥♥ Mostly♥♥♥♥♥♥though.
If you are thinking of buying this for the story, don't. If you are thinking of buything this game for crafting, don't. If you are thinking of buying this to feel like a badass mage that sets up the whole arena for a combo and nukes the ♥♥♥♥ out of everyone with one gloriously timed combo, absolutely don't. If you are thinking of buying this game for the visuals, then yeah. It does look good. I guess graphics is all their talent and focus went into. This is the worst and weakest I have felt as a mage in many many years. This game does the exact opposite of what it advertises.

On one hand, it's a real wholesome message for the kid that is trying to figure out his future occupation by playing job simulators ("Mommy, I don't want to be Mayor because City Builder X-s servers kept crashing on me!"). On the other hand, if you are wierdo like me who plays games to have fun you are going to find very little of that here as the game becomes increasingly more depressive. This is compounded by the fact that you have no sense of agency while you are helplessly observing your character making dumb decisions and throwing his life away.
FINAL VERDICT: If you are looking to have fun, this ain't the game to do it.

Alright, I've got a story to tell.
A long time ago, I got an xbox 360. It was an amazing system. At the time the graphics were fine for someone just getting into video games and the game lineup was amazing, at the time, as I said.
I got a few months of Gold membership on said xbox 360, which later extended to 2 or so years as I was getting into the system.
Then, out of nowhere, the game Mafia II became the free Games with Gold for the month.
I was first relucent to try it out, as it seems like one of the boring FPS/TPS genres (I don't even know how.)
I, one day, went to my xbox 360 downloads to try it out. At first, the game seemed like the regular linear story focused games. I then went in, crushed in more hours, played it more, and sooner or later, I was hooked.
By hooked, I mean, super hooked. Like Sid Meier's Civilization 5 or World of Warcraft fanatic hooked.
So, then I played countless hours of the game, as I said before, crushing in more time and playing a lot more.
I learned then the game could be played non linear if you do it the right way.
Instead of getting money like a regular person, I started to rob gun stores for their money and weapons, and others just to immerse the experience of a game not supposed to be open world, but my imagination at the time prompted it to be.
Let me just say to you all right now, this is, I repeat, not linear if you imagine it as an open world game.
I treated this game like one would treat Grand Theft Auto V, in a way. It became one of the best experiences, and it also lowered my GTA V story mode playtime (Due to the fact I could have fun on this game as well.) It was a fun time I had. I didn't even want the DLC. I had enough fun in the base game.
So then, there came a time that the Xbox 360 came to show it's age, as you can see from some last gen ports nowadays, and it was a time to sell it. I found a good deal at a local Gamestop to get an xbox one, GTA V, and an extra controller (One of the selling points as I loved couch co-op), if you traded in an xbox 360, all for $300 USD.
I proceeded to get an Xbox One.
Once I got it, I quickly went into the story mode of GTA V, the game I got with the One. It was a fun time, yes, but it lacked the feel of Mafia II that made me sad inside. I got a lot of other games too, but none matched Mafia II in terms of fun (Except for Just Cause 3, I guess, but that is a different story.)
And then came the announcement for backwards compatibility
I basically almost threw up. I was so happy at the announcement, I didn't care if Mafia II was coming or not, I just wanted to see it.
Then I saw the lineup.
Most games I didn't have, but I saw a few I loved (Just Cause 2 being a favorite of mine, as well as Battleblock Theater), but I still wished Mafia II would someday come.
I waited, and waited.
Today is July 29th, 2016, and it still hasn't came.
I thought it would be quick, since 2k supported the compat, but it didn't come.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Along came the Humble Bundle, savior of men.
It offered a whole bunch of 2k games, but all I really cared about was Mafia II (And I guess a few others). The Director's cut no less.
Let me just say, as soon as I scrapped the money, I bought the bundle.
I basically cried, of joy. I finally had Mafia II back in my heart and soul.
I was so happy to see it. (Even though it plays at 15-20 fps on all lows 480p, but it still is surprisingly playable for me.)
I am amazed how this game isn't as popular as Grand Theft Auto, because it deserves the praise.
The mafia games are in no doubt for me the best mafia games ever (I never played The Godfather 2, as insane as that, and so I cannot rank it), but I cannot recommend this game enough.
It takes about 30-60 minutes to be able to be free and "Free roam" even though you do still have objectives.
It was an amazing game for it's time, and I actually don't know why people still don't have this game.
TL;DR how the crap do you not already have this game, it's amazing and arguably better then gta 4. could be worth 20 dollars if you have an imagination
TL;DR the tl;dr: buy this game

Imagine a castle building game where you build dense walls to survive hordes of enemies, and use soldiers and catapults to repel their swelling mass at your doorstep. That is not this game. At least not the way that you might imagine it.
I am aware that the game is still in beta when making this review and I can forgive things like work queue locking up, or the path finding of the workers taking them around the map instead of through the door I built for them. However, that does not excuse the terrible selection process, which is pivotal and my primary gripe.
I purchase the game over 6 months ago, played it, got frustrated with it, but I did not condemn it. I reserved my opinion with the it's beta status in mind. So I came back recently, hoping that game had advanced and ironed out the problems. They did advance it and supply two game modes instead of one, and some prefabbed worlds, however my biggest issue still remained.
Selecting your units is hit or miss, at best. Don't trust the drag select box. and don't trust shift/ctrl selecting either. You have select individuals and give them commands as individuals... assuming you can select them. The cursor will hover right above the intended target and somehow the hit box is not responding. So if you're ever in a pinch and you need to move your workers, might as well kiss them goodbye. You click frantically to simply select them and they die in the process after one hit.
It was very frustrating seeing how my next issue is with the recruiting of new units. Maybe I'm missing something, but I've two dozen little stars floating around my crystal... why are they ALL used to make ONE unit? When later on there are only a few stars and it seems to be enough for that one unit. Hell, sometimes I've got plenty of stars and I can't make a unit. It was inconsistent and made no sense.
The game otherwise is fine. Not really edge of you seat type stuff, but it fills whatever child-hood need there is to build massive structures with nothing but blocks, and then see it crash down when you knock it down. Not much in the sound department, and the graphics are very bright and friendly. I wish the enemies had more to offer, however since it's really easy to bottle neck them and shower them with arrows.
With the problems, and low replay value, I can't recommend this game.

As a game designer I decided to approach this from a game design point of view. The game is overally pretty nice and features great art and animation, music, semi good mechanics, and some ocassionally passable and really unnessecary voice acting. It's major pit falls are in the story, some mechanics, and level design.
I wont harp on about the things I like too much as they should be pretty easy to see by watching gameplay. The art looks great and there is lots of fantastic detail. One of my favorite parts is the tv screens that appear way off in the distance on the final levels. Mechanics are okay and it's neat that the game features different playstyles for each character. Personally my favorite to play is Milla but Lilac is okay as well if you really want to get through the game quickly so you can scratch it off your to-play list.
The biggest problem I have with the game is the level design. Levels are non-linear which would be great in most platforms but fails hard here as it forces you to slow down and figure out where to go (not a good feature in a game based off Sonic). There are some interesting intersecting hills (going up and down on different layers) but it's extremely difficult to change which path you are on as you can randomly fall through ramps. Some levels feature instant kill traps (a cardinal sin a game design) which are just infrequent enough to punish you for trying to look around and ruin a no-death run if you failed to memorize the level completely. If possible I would remove these from any sequels and just deal a large chunk of damage to the player and respawn them outside the trap. Be aware that jumping can randomly cause you to start running on the ceiling when trying to do more delecate manouvering. Also don't jump when going uphill as you lose all spend and get sent backwards because your jump direction is exactly perpendicular to the ground. After mechanics the story is crap, it reads like a bad fanfic and alot of characters (such as Spade, Zao, Magistrate, Pandas) are completely unessecary. It seems none of the characters really have a story motivate or if they do (Milla and seeing her family agian) it is completely forgotten.
Overall I wouldn't really recommend the game unless you really want a platformer and can deal with a few rookie game dev mistakes, I'd just stick with classic mode (no story) if I were you.

This is basically a remake of Caesar III but with several downgrades. The buildings look like they are from 1980 graphics, building spaces are based on a 2x2 area like In Zeus or Emperor and not like the 1x1 square system in Caesar and Pharoah, even roads take up a 2x2 area. The developers did not fix the walker issues that were present in C3 and Pha despite this issue being somewhat resolved in the later games. The first two levels seems almost a complete remake of C3's campaign. The store page says that it's inspired by C3, but what it appears to be is a complete rip of the original game with no new additions other than low quality graphics. I would highly avoid wasting time with this game and go back to basics with the Fantasic Four: Caesar III, Pharaoh, Zeus, Emperor.

This is less of a review and more of a reccomendation.  And it's to stay well away.  Firstly, the game is rather unpolished.  The user interface is rough and my character floats an inch or so off the ground.  Combat and quests are very much sameish.  Hub-based ! quests and combat that requires you to stay completely still (even changing the angle of the camera or your character's facing stops your current action).  Menus are sometimes confusing to navigate and the game seems as though it was translated from another language entirely (and poorly at that).  Attention to detail is abysmally low (I read that a dummy dodged my blow and I'll reckon that structures as well might do that.)
The game has a stat system, but that only attempts to pidgeonhole the player into a certain race/faction in order to play a class they're interested in to its potential.  There are hints of a crafting system but I couldn't get far enough in before the game disconnected me and I just don't have the heart to launch it again.

DISCLAIMER: This game was release in 2000, making it 17 years old.  I AM NOT reviewing Final Fantasy IX as a *game*; why would I have to say about a game that's nearly as old as I was when I played it the first time?  I'm reviewing it as a *remake*, and how I feel about the quality of that remake.  Seeing as people are taking this review personally, I figured I'd point that out directly.
If what you are looking for is a chance to revisit FFXI with Steam support?  This is what you're looking for.  However, just know that it is a downgrade from the PSX version.
I had upwords of 80 hours clocked into that PSX version.  So while my playtime (at time of writing) is under an hour?  This is a game I know very well...and the issues with this new Steam version are obvious from minute one.  For starters, the new and polished character models make the old, unpolished, PSX backgrounds look horrible.  Sometimes this can be largely ignored, but at other times it looks unavodiably ugly.  You don't have to be a graphics/FPS snob to really get put off by this.  Screenshots don't do the issue justice; look on Youtube for some footage, as the issue becomes most apparent when you see it in real time.  It's hard for me to overstate how awful this looks; it drops the backgrounds into the uncanny valley, making it look like wonderfully crafted models are performing in front of a construction paper background.  Seriously disappointing.
Controls and interface are also not feeling quite right.  Instead of full analog support, you can only move in the 8 cardinal directions.  This makes movement feel akward and inpercise.  The menu layout feel like they needed a bit more play testing, as it feels a touch unintuitive.  Neither of these issues are deal breakers, but it feels weird to see a game get more difficult to control when the original had no problems in this regard.
Let's be clear that a *lot* of my issues with this release are with the price point and how it makes the lack of effort put into the PC Port all the more galling.  Square-Enix is charging 21 dollars (at time of writing, that is it's non-sale price) for a game that launched almost 16 years ago.  It should be an embarassment to Square Enix that someone can go on-line, right now, and find brand new copies of this game on E-Bay...for less then the price of the digital release.
This isn't a game lost to time, or too rare to find elsewhere; the original is still readily available, while this new version is a lazy port, released in such an unprofessional state that it makes a good arguement for piracy and emulation.  A lower price point for what is here would be reasonable.  A better port at this price would have been reasonable.  A PSX Final Fantasy bundle on Steam, which collectively reduces their price, would even be a welcome alternative to what we have here.  My opinion is that SE dropped the ball big time; the Steam version could have been nothing more than copies of the FFIX .ISO files and it would have been a more solid and consistant experience.
What this game does add in terms of polish and options doesn't excuse the lackluster cash-grab result that is on display here.  If you can get it on sale?  It might be worth it, depending on how much you like PSX-era Square games.  I bought it during the 2016 Steam Christmas Sale, and at that price?  It is acceptable.  At full price, however, without a specific reason to want the steam version?  This is a complete and utter failure and I do not recomend it.  The charm, the story, the characters....all of that is still on display.  However, they all were there 17 years ago too; this version has a tough time justifying it's own existance.

I've yet to see a Sonic style game... or any platformer for that matter, that has impressed me as much as Freedom Planet has.
This game is truly something special, I didn't think much of it when I first saw it but the more I found myself craving something akin to Sonic the Hedgehog 2, the more I wanted to give this a shot.
What did I find within this game that made me think it so special?
Let's begin:
Story:
The story is actually kind of decent, or at the very least I don't mind it being there. The game has voice acted cutscenes and the voice work is pretty nice and fits the mood of the characters, though Milla gets the helium voice acting scene a little too well. The story can be entirely bypassed too so it isn't a total obstruction... although not doing the story makes it seem like you are just going from place to place because video game.
Music:
This game has a soundtrack that just oozes with goodness. The third level "Fortune Night" in particular has a theme that is just ear melting. The explosions from destroying bosses are also spectacularly satisfying. I have no complaints here.
Gameplay:
This game has a sonic style of game play, and that is quite fine. It takes all of the best parts of Sonic 2 and 3 and blends them with an attack button and a focus on both platforming and action. I'll admit that this game can get soulcrushing with its difficulty, this being very noticable during boss battles where tiny mistakes can get you obliterated instantly. The game has three playable characters, Lilica, Carol, and Milla. Each character has a unique focus and playstyle.
Lilac is very traditional platforming and is the one to go with if you are new. She has a boost technique and a brutal double jump attack so she is able to keep punishment on enemies with a fair amount of ease.
Carol is liken to playing as a ninja of sorts. She trades a traditional double jump for a wall jump and has a high focus on just being a fast attacker. She can get a bike that adds to her moveset quite well and the sense of speed with her is very high.
Milla is my personal favorite despite her many problems. Milla has very low health, but her attacks are really useful during boss battles. She uses a shield that can be fired like a beam, and the shield can reflect boss attacks back at them so ranged bosses can be cheesed to hell by her. She also has a flutter jump that makes platforming a joke for her. Just remember that she has the health of a wet napkin. Getting hit as her is PAINFUL and it can totally render you moot.
Boss battles are frantic and never stop moving. Battles aren't very slow and its a dance between who even has control during the fight. My personal favorite boss being the one in Fortune Night because of the constant feeling of speed.
That's really one of this games biggest pros, its speed. You feel like a badass when you clear a stage lightning fast because this game rarely has roadblocks preventing you from charging forward at the speed of sound.
This game is a special sort of gem, and as such it gets a 9.5/10 from me.

Absolver, that one punching game.
This is just some of my thoughts about the game so far.
First of I'm just going to put it here that yes, the game does make you feel like this awesome martial artist badass.
Absolver is one of those games where people will label it as a "Dark Souls" type of games. In a way, it feels like it but I can assure you it's not.
Absolver is straight up a melee only game, so far I haven't encountered an archer type NPC, thus making it exciting but at the same time difficult. At least the game doesn't punish you, the only punishment is that you have to trek back to the place you just died and encounter the NPC you killed (not sure if NPC respawns after death sometimes it does other times it doesn't). The beauty of this is that the game encourages you to keep fighting, cause the more you fight the more experience you get both literally and figuratively.
The literal part is that you can learn a new move by simply fighting an NPC, players or your mentors even, it slowly adds experience in the circle bar.
Yes, you can be a Jedi and teach your Padawans.
The combat of the game feels fluid and yes it feels amazing. at first its kinda tricky to understand the combat mechanics on how the four stance work and the combat deck, oh god that took me awhile to figure out what it means, but eventually, after screwing around a bit, you'll get used to it and have a certain feel on what kind of combos you want to build in your stance.
Lock-on feature in the game is simple but at times it does get glitchy as ♥♥♥♥ by that I mean, it lock-off from an NPC or players and targets an NPC that's not even in range. Just like the combat mechanic after screwing around for a bit, not only is it easy to use but in a fight against multiple NPC or players, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ being able to switch targets on the fly and focusing down on all of them gives of this badass feeling, like one of those kung fu movies.
So far interaction with the others "seamless" players, game alerts you at the bottom right telling you who you're playing with, really depends on you. I've encountered players that roam around the area with me and basically tag team the NPC. Its actually fun and no I haven't met any players who wanted to fight, maybe because it just release, but regardless how they made the multiplayer for the game is great but the connection for it sucks♥♥♥♥♥ No, it literally sucks♥♥♥♥♥ I had the NPC killing me when I was running away, after realising they're teleporting everywhere, from them and just straight up died back at the spot I encountered them originally.
So yeah the biggest issue is definitely the connection. Don't bother setting the online option to invitation only, whenever you enter a new area or zone, it'll reset back to its default.
This is just an early thoughts of what I was observing and feeling when playing the game. I'll make an actual review when I beat the game.

If you liked Mafia I (which I did), you'll enjoy this, as it's more of the same, with slightly updated graphics and a story set in the 1940s/50s instead of the 1930s.  Shooting and driving mechanics are decent, if limited (no blind fire for instance).  While I enjoyed the story and setting, with it's beautiful cars and humorous dialogue from some great voice actors, the whole game was way too linear and short.  Most of my time spent in the game was just driving around looking at the city of Empire Bay and getting into car chases with the cops to see how long I could last at max wanted status.  Played through only to mid-way point when it first came out and only just finished after starting over a few days ago in preparation for the third game.
There were zero side missions or dynamic events outside of a few NPC conversations you can stumble across, so other than wandering around to just look at stuff, or steal cars/rob stores and then get in epic infinitely spawning police battles and/or car chases, there was really no point in going off the plot railroad.  No building a power base, no raising influence with mob bosses, no hits, no point to even earning money except when a story mission required it.  You buy clothes (to hide your identity if wanted or to look snazzy), you buy guns (but you don't need to since every mission gives weapons by the truckload), and you buy repaints/repairs/plate changes for your stolen cares (to lose wanted status), but since you can just steal another car, again, not much point.
In a game with such a well-developed environment with expansive draw distance and tons of NPCs, cars and varied terrain, I expected there to be something to do besides the one at a time story missions.  Seems like a waste of resources not to use most of the city.
A+ for the vintage Playboy centerfolds scattered throughout the story.  F for the female character models, which looked hideous, especially in the cutscenes.  Have the developers never actually seen a real woman before?  Like in real 3-dimensional life?  I know they've seen them in magazines and I know they can render passable male character models, but the women looked like they had been made by aliens.
I didn't bother with the DLC, because LOL, $10 each?  If they added actual side missions to the main game with Vito and breathed some purpose into the massive map, sure, but more short story missions with Joe or Jimmy?  Who cares about them?  Pass.
I had fun and don't regret getting the game, but I'd only recommend the vanilla version if it's on sale.  Game's six years old and the new one is right around the corner.

[edit below]
Some games just can't be simplified by "Thumbs Up" or "Thumbs Down", this is one such case. So I save "Not Reccomended" cases to games that are busted, broken, bad DLC practices, harmful policies toward customers and similar cases. Major/Minor doesn't fall into any of those categories.`
So, you're reading this to know whether you should buy it or not, let's start addressing the elephant in the room (pun kinda intended):
-Eee
furry
This issue tend to plague a LOT of things. I've had my share of heated discussions about Dust AET or Zootopia, those are two examples of awesome games/movies that people dismiss for thinking that "it is furry". News flash, when aiming for a rated E genre, something meant for all ages, a fantasy world is required. How to better to unbind ourselves of reality than not having human-like characters? Walt Disney knew that, look at his characters. Most kids show tend to use this, it's not something new, nor it's something "furry"
But Major/Minor might not look like it's neutral nor like it's a kid's game, does it? Indeed, the game page adverstises that “
” And that's not something it would appeal to anyone who isn't a furry.
it also says that Major/Minor is "
". If you're anything like me, you'll think this is a tall order to beat, but it'll definitely pique your curiosity.
So yes, the game
indeed "furry", if you're part of that fandom the game will easily appeal to you, but what if you're not? Then there's two cases, either you'll be the purebreed hater (which by no means will read any review marked as "Reccomended", making this part pretty pointless) or the regular guy who doesn't care about "furry fandom" and neither having anthro characters. Believe it or not, this is where I am. I mentioned Zootopia and Dust because those are two things I love, and it angers me people dismissing it due to having anthropomorphic characters, no one cares about the beautiful story, artworks, characters or moral lessons in those, only how they look. That's just sad.
But I'm deviasting from the topic at hand. For those who do not consider themselves furries, and would have no interest in a visual novel just because of a specific fandom, how does Major/Minor fares? It definitely doesn't come close to the overall quality P4, Steins Gate or Tales of Symphonia has, but there are clear references of it in the game. Think of it like this, if you've played any of those, odds are your brain thought of some "branches" that weren't explored in the games. This game's developer gathered those ideas and made his own game. But how does it compare to those other games? There's some clear references, right in the beggining of the game, you'll be greeted into the
Ark and not much longer after that you'll know about the Midnight
Murders. At that point I wondered if I was about to play a furry re-telling of Persona, but not long after that the game took a drastic turn, taking you to another world entirely. After 3 hours into the Novel, I can say that the story references those games while being it's own thing.
The problem of a Visual Novel, is that you don't really know whether it's good or not until you've read the whole history, and I'm not there yet. But here's what I CAN say about it:
+ Does a good job using aspects of other stories while still being original
+ Story branches are very well done, not every VN can make such radical changes at how the branches play out.
+ OST is catchy. Some VN's are plagued by annoying songs, however that does vary from people to people.
+ Good diversity of characters. (Personally, it reminded me of Borderlands 2)
- Character artwork is a bit awkward at first glance
- No characters animations/emotions, meaning sometimes they break some sad news to you while smirking. It breaks the immersion a little.
- No custom saves or interims. Meaning the game decides when to save for you.
- Quick text skip is still too slow if you're re-doing large sections
So the bottom line is: I suppose this game is great if you're interested in the furry fandom, disposable if you outright hate it. And if you're somewhere in between, liking VNs while not caring about being furry or not,

Major\Minor is a decidedly furry visual novel.
You begin the game in Tokyo, having just arrived there for the first time. You learn that you have been granted the power of saving and loading the game, which makes you a very important person. The story quickly gets more complex and never fails to surprise.
Most of the game is spent reading dialogue over illustrations of the scene and characters, while occasionally making game-affecting decisions. The character designs and the accompanying artwork are cute and well made, but perhaps not everybody's cup of tea. I found it charming!
The game has been called a dating sim, but I'm sad to say that thus far, five chapters in, Major\Minor hasn't provided me with a virtual animal boyfriend. Fortunately, I find myself quite hooked on the bizarre story, and I'm constantly interested and excited to see what happens next.
This game appeals most to quite a niche audience, but if you're into furries and visual novels, go for it!

This is a very enjoyable game which is worth picking up, provided you know what to expect.
Do not expect non-linearity, particularly varied enemies, or a deep plot.
Do expect a wonderfully engaging crafting system, beautiful scenery and competent voice acting, and unbelievably satisfying spell-slinging.
The new 'smart inventory' system works beautifully to get you into the game (as long as you poke your head into the journal to look up a few concepts now and then) enough to begin crafting your own spells. I typically don't like crafting-focused games too much - I generally want to be able to pick stuff up and hit a "optimise" button to equip the best stuff. This handles that nicely - if you craft a spell, the smart inventory will then provide an upgrade button when appropriate, making inventory management simple. If even that level of crafting puts you off, you can treat the default spells as abilities to be mixed, matched, and upgraded, never diving into the deep spell crafting system underneath. With this approach you'd end up using, say, fire for damage, ice for crowd control, and kinesis to apply mastery (play the game to find out that *that* means).
The combat is not hugely varied, but is consistently challenging and scales well - smacking down demons in the later stages which were Big Bosses earlier on is immensely gratifying. The minions only have a few flavours and types - melee, ranged, spellcasters, flying, and tanks. Even on lower difficulties this is sufficient to provide a consistent challenge, although it is a little repetitive and it's rare that the environment provides any interesting tactical options beyond ducking behind cover.
If you can get this at a discount ($10 or so) it's entirely worth it.

I love this game. It looks beautiful, it sounds beautiful, and it plays beautiful. Your character controls very well, and you usually have a lot of options on how to complete each level. The music is a lovely mix between instruments and chip-tune sounds. The art style is very pleasing to look at. The levels aren't long, but the fun comes from trying to find the perfect path to beat the level as fast as possible. Not only does this offer great replay value, but there's tons of clever community-made and dev-made levels on the workshop. The level editor is included so you can even try your hand at making your own. The story isn't much, but it flows with the gameplay in a very clever way. your character is comatose and is trying to escape the world inside her dreams, where all the levels take place. And that's where the genius merging of gameplay and story comes in. This game gets REALLY hard later on. The final levels are ridiculous. The DLC levels are soul-crushingly difficult. You will experience a range of emotions that very few games can produce. The frustration builds and turns into desperation, then rage, then sadness as you let go of the mouse and stop playing. These levels give you a great insight to the emotions of your protagonist as she is desperately fighting her way through the broken fortresses with no clear goal in sight. The satisfaction you get from completing a tricky level is more than worth the frustration it put you through. If you like a challenging and fast paced 3D platformer, pick this up with the Defiance DLC, and the soundtrack if you can afford it. It has a few flaws, but this game is easily a solid 8/10 for the non-casual crowd.

Cloudbuild is a combination of Dark Souls frustration and DeadCore-like speed.
The Graphics are semi-unique and look really good on their own. There seems to be a story but to be honest you don't really follow it since you have to beat each level to progress the story, and if you try to get at least A on every track, that could take time. The only think that I have to address negatively is something so simple yet so frustrating.. It's not even the sometimes wonky transitions from wallruns etc... Rather its the strange decision to force the player to press "space" after a climb to not hang on the ledge. This is really frustrating because if you are dashing up a wall and want to continue, you have to press space everytime you reach the top. It you press to late, its ok, she'll just hang in there and you lose at max half a second. But if you press to early, and thats the real issue here, you will jump away from the wall, most likely killing that run. It's just a weird choice to force the player to press space.. every.. time. I would give it a solid 10/10 if it werent for this issue. The Soundtrack is good and even after hours of listening to it, it kind of never really gets boring. The pace is fun and there are often multiple ways to finish a level depending on your playstyle. Enemy's sometimes really are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥but once you get yourself to shoot at them rather to try to evade their attacks it makes alot more fun.  So to sum things up, I would give it a 8/10 because the space issues really made me rage more times then it actually should. But for the price now (Steam Summer Sale) It's really worth a grab.

Final Fantasy IX is one of the best games in the formerly-awesome Final Fantasy series.  This is an excellent port.  New functionalities have been added, such as no-encounters mode, fast forward, auto battle, keyboard, mouse, and controller support, autosave (as well as a ton of regular save slots), an option to turn off extended battle cam and a handful of integrated cheat modes.  These additions fix all the annoying parts of the original release without taking anything away from the game.  The high-res graphics options make the 3d character models much clearer while still retaining their original looks.
On top of all these changes, FF9 is just a great game.  It's very easy to lose yourself in the gigantic game world, the well-paced, engrossing story, colorful visuals and loads of great characters.  For first time players, this is an excellent entry point into the Final Fantasy franchise, and for returning players wondering if its worth it, it is.

This game is perfect for anyone who wants a 2D Sonic experience, likes to fight hard bosses, or just likes the overall design aspect of Sonic characters themselves. I know Freedom Planet is its own thing, but referencing Sonic will give people (who haven't played the game) a general idea of how it plays.
Freedom Planet caters to all audiences, whether this is your first video game to even the most seasoned of veteran gamers, there's a difficulty mode for you. But all games have their flaws. Here are the major Pros and Cons I have found in the game.
Cons
Some of the voice acting is a bit off.
- I understand that they did not record the lines in a studio and did it in the comfort of their own homes but, some of the lines could have been a little better. Especially when they are in a very dramatic moment and it seems the characters are speaking normally.
Milla’s shield isn’t the best.
- This just might be my user error, but a lot of the time I find projectiles get trapped between Milla and her shield. This happens often with shade troopers, they get right up in your face then shoot.
It's hard to dodge some attacks as Milla
- Sometimes as Milla it is very hard to dodge some attacks that Lilac and Carol can easily pass through.  Lilac and Carol have a special attacks that grant them invincibility for the duration of the move. Milla does not have this. Her special spawns a blocks that reflects most projectiles, but doesn’t protect from melee attacks and lasers.
There is not enough character development
- Most of the time is spent during gameplay. Although the cutscenes are quite long sometimes, not enough character development is given. This leads to us knowing very little about the characters themselves.

Pros
The music and visuals are great!
- If you are a long time Sonic fan 2D or 3D, you will love the music in this game. The music is high quality and really matches with the theme of each stage. A major boss battle feels like a major boss battle, and the visuals are just amazing.
There are so many extras.
- Galaxy Trail has put so much love and care into this game. From the collectible cards to Majong, they have filled this game to the brim with unique and cool extras. Also the menu screen can shake. :)
Every character feels unique.
- Every character in Freedom Planet has an entirely unique move set from one another. This makes each character feel truly unique and keeps each story fun. Unlike Classic Sonic gameplay which is more of a copy and paste with added moves.
The boss fights are fun.
- Sure it doesn’t make people feel good when they are getting torn to shreds by a boss, but the bosses in Freedom Planet feel like they are manageable because they have very obvious attack patterns. They usually do a ton of damage, but these attack patterns makes it a bit easier. It feels very satisfying to defeat a hard boss with little to no damage taken after learning it’s attack pattern.
To me the pros outweigh the cons by a lot. Overall I think Freedom Planet is a good buy for any Sonic fan, or any gamer in general. I do not recommend this however, for anyone who doesn't like platformers or challenging games. (This game can be pretty tough sometimes)
- Now let's all get ready for Freedom Planet 2! -

Growing up playing the original sonic games, this gem was a real throwback to my childhood. The gameplay is smooth with responsive controls, the pixel art is simply gorgious, the story (while the cutscenes might be a bit long a filleresque for my taste, like something out of metalgear solid) is enthralling and emotional and you have a profound sense of accomplishment when you see the end credits scroll across the screen. And let's face it, when your main playable characters are a literal freakin dragon!!, a spunky motorcycle riding wildcat and an absolutely adorable doggy with a Yoshi style jump and an energy shield that shoots lazers, you've got yourself an infinity out of 10 game.
For anyone who wants a great classic style modern platformer game, this is by far the most epic you'll find on the steam store. It's worth way more than the $17.00 it's sold for.

A Sonic fan game that decides to do its own thing.
Story:
Story is straight forward enough with an evil alien crash landing on the planet and plans to put the three kingdoms against each other so he can get away with their power source: the Kingdom Stone. The game really begins when our heroes, Lilac and Carol, notice some helicopters chasing a plane of some kind and chase after it, meeting an alien named Torque and with the help of a young dog name Milia, the two agree to help him stop the evil Lord Brevon.
I'll be honest, it takes a while for the story to really get going. Sure, after finishing level 2, the story actually has a decent pace to it but it feels like some establishment of Lilac and Carol's past was messing because we met this guy called Spade and I was like "who is this and why are you making such a big deal over him". Then there was the Red Scarves stuff which I have no idea what that was about and something happening between our heroes and Spade and I just didn't care. And Spade gets hit the worst since he barely felt like his involvement matter to the story even though his brother is one of the main villains.
But like I said earlier, the rest of the story is fine even if it drags on a bit and rest of the cast were okay. I understood Milia from her first real cutscene in the game than I did about Carol and Lilac throughout most of the game.
Gameplay:
While the level and art design might make you think this plays like a Sonic game, but it doesn't. For a Sonic fan like myself, it took a while for me to get use to it since you can't roll down hills and enemies don't die in one hit. So first impressions weren't great but by the time I got to Relic Maze Act 2, I started to like it.
For playable characters, we start with Lilac who was the only one I played on Normal difficulty. She okay to play with a nice double jump attack which is useful against most foes including bosses and their's her dragon boost move which can send her flying in one direction but it's difficult to aim as she can ricochet of walls. While these are useful, you have limited energy that means you'll have to wait a few seconds before you can use it again and make do with your normal melee attacks.
Then there's Carol that I didn't like playing as much. sure she's the only one that can roll down hills and can wall jump on walls but I didn't like playing as her much since I find her attacks more annoying than fun and she has this leap move instead of a double jump which doesn't help much except maybe make me fall to my death if there were that many bottomless pits. She only becomes fun when she gets her motorbike which turns her into Lilac except instead of a dragon boost, she can drive up walls. Shame it gets destroyed quickly except for two boss fights.
And finally Milia. She's my favourite as although she has less health than the other two, she can flutter jump, summon cubes to throw at foes and make a small blast of energy, plus she has this cool move when you summon a cube and fire it with the blast creates a laser beam that can do a lot of damage. Oh, yeah, every character has their own move list. I just didn't care as the basic moves got me through just fine. Anyway, while she's more of a traditional platformer than the rest since her low health means she has to be more careful, I was enjoying myself more fluttering over my enemies and hitting them with cubes.
Also there's a bullet hell section. Fine for Lilac, sucks fore everyone else. And can I ask why Brevon is the only boss with a health bar?
Presentation:
At first I wasn't that impressed with the presentation. Sure the character design screams Sonic only males also wear clothes and we see the Asian theme their going with, the first level really didn't wow me with its music or theme and the second level was the same. I was actually thinking of stop playing it since both the gameplay and presentation weren't doing anything for me and I haven't unlocked Milia.
Then Relic Maze act 2 happened when I went down that mine shaft, everything went into a beautiful shade of blue and this brilliant song started playing. After that, the rest of the game followed with wonderful Asian and mechanical settings and one good track per level. Even the bosses became a spectacle as while the first boss was just a robot snake, soon you'll face giant mantis and get chased by a robot panther soon after. There's even a fight where the whole is dark and you have to face this giant beast, so big that you're the size of it's eye.
And of course I have to give a brief comment on the voice acting. It's fine. No bad performance's though Torque voice isn't the best quality. And there's clear effort in it as the lines are said well and Lilac deserves special mention as when she gets emotional, she gets emotional.
Verdict:
I must say this again that this is not Sonic. I know there are people who think this is the true successor to Sonic but it isn't. It Is it's own thing with it's own style and no matter of telling it to skin the Sonic series and start wearing said skin should make it change its mind.

I don't normally write reviews, but this was just absurd.  I hope this demo isn't a good representation of what the actual game is like.  If it is, from what I've seen the game surely suffers from what I call "red keycard syndrome".  Red keycard syndrome is where a puzzle game, instead of providing you with a relatively linear path toward solving the puzzle, makes you wander around aimlessly.  You're forced to traverse the environment, spamming the interaction key over all surfaces until you find the magic button that makes the story progress.  Until that happens, you find yourself exploring and re-exploring the same environments over and over and over, to the piont where it actually consumes a majority of the playtime.  Part of immersion is a reasonable pace, and anything that needlessly disrupts the pace will detract from the immersion.  Many 90s and 00s games suffered from red keycard syndrome, including some Resident Evil games.  I'm sad to see it hasn't gotten any better.

FFIX is one of the more underrated entries in the series. At its original release, right after the more futuristic themed Final Fantasy 7 and 8, Final Fantasy 9 was meant to be a trip back to the series roots - with a fantasy setting, the return of the job system, and featuring a multitude of references paying homage to the older games in the series. The graphics are dated, but the art style still looks great - the world of Gaia is rich and detailed, with places I'd love to visit if they existed. Nobuo Uematsu knocks it out of the park with the soundtrack, with memorable songs to fit every situation, and some especially emotional pieces for some of the story's more important moments.
The story is well written with sharp dialogue and a frequent sense of humor. The leading guy, Zidane, is a cheerful everyman, a departure from the brooding leads of 7 and 8. The rest of the cast is likable too, from the naive Princess Garnet, the quiet young black mage Vivi, to the stuffy and stern royal knight Steiner, and everyone in between. This is one of the few RPGs where I also found the supporting cast just as interesting as the main party. Zidane's thief buddies great in particular, and wouldn't be at all out of place as playable characters.
As far as ports go, it's not bad but not great. It's functional, and I haven't experienced any showstopping crashes or bugs, but it's worth noting that there's no 60 FPS here, and it's letterboxed due to the original being made before everyone had widescreen displays. The pre-rendered backgrounds are still low resolution and blurry (not a lot they could do about that, short of redrawing the entire game) but the character models look hugely better than the original - you can see detail on the crisp, high resolution models that wasn't there on the original game's twitchy, pixelated characters. The loading times are also improved, particularly when entering battle, and the ability to turn off the dramatic camera panning at the beginning of every fight speeds things up nicely.
Like many of Square's PC releases, there are "boosts" available - if you feel like being cheesy, you can max out your money, levels, and abilities, super power your characters in battle, and so on. Some of the "cheats" are less gamebreaking though - like automatically learning abilities on newly-found equipment (less grinding), and temporarily disabling random encounters makes life easier when you're traveling through lower level areas filled with enemies that are little more than pests slowing you down. It's a competent port of a great game, and worth picking up if you're interested in a little JRPG history for your Steam library.

I bought the game a while ago and just started to play it.
Let me say what I think on the first hour of play: It is difficult. It is not a casual Megaman-esque experience. That said, it builds and improves even on the formulas of parkour and the shooting aspect is left as an afterthought.
The game starts you off in a very basic level, which isn't too crazy, but it also is not easy either. You have to scan your environment for the right path at first on the tutorial level. However, once the tutorial level is finished you will find out this is a multipath game where you have more than one way to finish things. You are going to be forced to scan your environment for platforms and alternate ways of overcoming a section of the level.
The AI in this game in so far as the few enemies you encounter is pretty easy. However, the entire game is not built for being a shooter. The parkour obstacles more than make up for the lack of an AI.
The controls are very good. In fact I have to say this is one of the best controller experiences I have had in videogames by far, and that is saying something. The fluidity of the graphics is also a plus, it manages to come out very strong in that department.
The music can keep you interested in this game for days if you are the kind of person who buys a game for its soundtrack. Definitely a good electronica mix going on in the game levels which keep your mind active.
The story are basically figments of data that are thrown at you after every mission, and it retells the experiences of a girl who apparently survived a massacre from an enemy robot/soldier. Not too fleshed out, but with these games you're not exactly expecting a story, you are expecting action, and in Cloudbuilt you have more than enough action.
All in all a good addition to any library that wants to get Megaman-esque experiences. It is not an action shooter, but it is a beautifully rendered game with a decent story nevertheless, with an interesting take on the parkour formula.
